title: Mersenne-Lambert ladder, gcd moments and Stern-Brocot geometry: where the #249 constant sits

concepts.label: Mersenne-Lambert transform L(f)
concepts.description: L(f) = sum_{d>=1} f(d)/(2^d - 1) = sum_n (f * zeta)(n) 2^{-n}, the Lambert series of an arithmetic function evaluated at r = 1/2.

concepts.label: The #249 constant S
concepts.description: S = sum_{n>=1} phi(n)/2^n, whose irrationality is Erdos problem #249 and is nowhere decided in this zone.

concepts.label: Primitive-conductor weight A = phi * mu
concepts.description: A(n) counts primitive Dirichlet characters of conductor n (OEIS A007431); A(p) = p - 2, A(p^e) = (p-1)^2 p^{e-2}, A >= 0.

concepts.label: Dirichlet convolution ladder
concepts.description: One convolution by zeta separates neighbouring rungs: A * zeta = phi, phi * zeta = Id, mu * zeta = eps, mu * Id = phi.

concepts.label: Fair-coin waiting-time reading
concepts.description: Doc-layer probabilistic gloss P(X = n) = 2^{-n}, P(d | X) = 1/(2^d - 1); no measure theory is invoked in the Lean statements.

concepts.label: Visible lattice point / coprime pair
concepts.description: Pairs (a,b) with gcd(a,b) = 1 on the addition antidiagonal a + b = n; their count is phi(n).

concepts.label: gcd-layer decomposition
concepts.description: Unique factorisation (a,b) = g*(a',b') with gcd(a',b') = 1, stratifying the positive quadrant by the value of the gcd.

concepts.label: Squared Lambert kernel L2
concepts.description: L2(f) = sum_d f(d)/(2^d - 1)^2, the two-variable (gcd) analogue of L, with divisor coefficient (f * Id) - (f * zeta).

concepts.label: Stern-Brocot mediant tree
concepts.description: The binary tree of reduced pairs under (a,b) -> (a+b, b) and (a,b) -> (a, a+b) rooted at (1,1).

concepts.label: Mersenne cylinder mass
concepts.description: M(a,b) = 1/((2^a - 1)(2^b - 1)), the closed form satisfying the exact mediant telescoping recursion.

concepts.label: Run / continuant coordinate
concepts.description: Alternating runs of mediant moves recoded as a continuant recurrence (A,B) -> (nA + B, A) with newest run first.

concepts.label: Fibonacci height scale
concepts.description: F_{r+3} is the exact minimum height of an r-run alternating word, attained on the all-unit spine.

concepts.label: Periodic Mersenne tail atom
concepts.description: omega_d(N) = 2^{N mod d}/(2^d - 1), the pointed coordinate of the primitive-conductor Lambert expansion.

concepts.label: Integral Euler/Witt coordinate
concepts.description: The normalised primitive coordinate A(n)/n and the question of a common integer index D clearing it.

concepts.label: Mobius incidence matrix
concepts.description: The finite jet matrix with entries mu((i+1)/(j+1)) when (j+1) | (i+1), unitriangular over Z.

concepts.label: Residual gauge on monomial minors
concepts.description: Column (or row-and-column) scalar weights W applied to a monomial matrix z_j^{e_i}; a diagonal action on determinants.

concepts.label: Dyadic parity after denominator clearing
concepts.description: If one dyadic exponent is uniquely largest and its numerator odd, the cleared common numerator is odd and hence nonzero.

concepts.label: Hankel moment determinant
concepts.description: Hankel matrices/determinants of a truncated signed q = 1/2 moment sequence; declared here as scaffolding only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any real weight w with |w(d)| <= d on positive arguments and any 0 <= r < 1, the double series over positive pairs regroups along divisor antidiagonals, giving sum_d w(d) r^d/(1-r^d) = sum_n (sum_{e|n} w(e)) r^n, sum_d w(d) r^d/(1-r^d)^2 = sum_n (sum_{e|n} w(e)(n/e)) r^n, and sum_d w(d) (r^d/(1-r^d))^2 = sum_n (sum_{e|n} w(e)(n/e - 1)) r^n. Summability rides the AM-GM majorant d*m <= d^2 + m^2.
statement_nodes.engine: signed linear-growth weighted Lambert pair regrouping (tsum_lambert_pair_regroup) over the divisor-antidiagonal sigma equivalence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The Lambert series identity sum_n f(n) x^n/(1-x^n) = sum_n (f*1)(n) x^n is classical (Lambert/Clausen). The only novelty is the hypothesis relaxation to signed weights of at most linear growth, which the module docstring states was needed because the kernel's landed weighted identity requires 0 <= w <= 1 and admits neither phi nor mu.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A = phi * mu (Dirichlet convolution) is multiplicative, satisfies A * zeta = phi, so sum_{e|n} A(e) = phi(n); A(p^k) = phi(p^k) - phi(p^{k-1}), A(p) = p - 2, A(p^2) = (p-1)^2, A(2) = 0, A >= 0 pointwise, and A(n) <= phi(n).
statement_nodes.engine: Mobius inversion via Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction convolution and multiplicative factorisation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A(n) is the standard count of primitive Dirichlet characters of conductor n, OEIS A007431; every value listed here is textbook character theory.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Elementary Mobius facts used by the ladder: |mu(n)| <= 1; sum_{e|n} mu(e) = [n = 1]; sum_{e|n} mu(e)(n/e) = phi(n); and the totient recast as an integer-valued arithmetic function.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: mu * zeta = eps and mu * Id = phi are the two standard Mobius inversions; Mathlib already owns the underlying lemmas.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{d>=1} phi(d) r^d/(1-r^d) = sum_{n>=1} n r^n; in particular sum_{d>=1} phi(d)/(2^d - 1) = 2 exactly.
statement_nodes.engine: signed linear-growth Lambert engine with w = phi, then phi * zeta = Id and sum n x^n = x/(1-x)^2
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Direct specialisation at x = 1/2 of the classical totient Lambert identity sum phi(n) x^n/(1-x^n) = x/(1-x)^2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{d>=1} mu(d) r^d/(1-r^d) = r; in particular sum_{d>=1} mu(d)/(2^d - 1) = 1/2 exactly.
statement_nodes.engine: signed linear-growth Lambert engine with w = mu, then mu * zeta = eps
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Specialisation at x = 1/2 of the classical identity sum mu(n) x^n/(1-x^n) = x.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{d>=1} A(d) r^d/(1-r^d) = sum_{n>=1} phi(n) r^n with A = phi * mu >= 0; at r = 1/2 this says the #249 constant S = sum phi(n)/2^n equals the positive Erdos-Borwein-shaped series sum_{d>=1} A(d)/(2^d - 1). The identity relocates #249 into the positive Mersenne-reciprocal family; it decides nothing about irrationality.
open_antecedents: irrationality of sum_{n>=1} phi(n)/2^n (Erdos #249) is unproved; the identity transports it to the equally unproved irrationality of sum_{d>=1} A(d)/(2^d - 1)
whether the Erdos 1948 congruence mechanism tolerates a weight with A(p) = p - 2 is not proved anywhere in the corpus (stated as open in the module docstring)
statement_nodes.engine: signed linear-growth Lambert engine with w = A, then A * zeta = phi
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The module docstring itself records the L(A) = S form at OEIS A256936/A007431; it is Mobius inversion of the classical totient Lambert identity.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{d>=1} mu(d) r^d/(1-r^d)^2 = sum_{n>=1} phi(n) r^n (via mu * Id = phi); at r = 1/2 this gives S = 1/2 + sum_{d>=1} mu(d)/(2^d - 1)^2, together with absolute convergence of both Mersenne and squared-Mersenne Mobius series. Equivalently the level-2 Mobius rung L2(mu) = S - 1/2.
open_antecedents: irrationality of sum_{d>=1} mu(d)/(2^d - 1)^2 is unproved and is equivalent to Erdos #249 by this identity
statement_nodes.engine: signed linear-growth squared-Lambert engine with w = mu, plus the split 2^d/(2^d-1)^2 = 1/(2^d-1) + 1/(2^d-1)^2
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Mobius inversion of the same classical totient Lambert identity, in squared-kernel dress; the module docstring calls it a lens, not progress.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every natural B there is a prime p with A(p) > B; hence no uniform natural bound holds for the primitive-conductor weight A.
statement_nodes.engine: A(p) = p - 2 plus infinitude of primes (Nat.exists_infinite_primes)
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Immediate from A(p) = p - 2 and Euclid. The docstring frames this as 'the exact obstruction to feeding primWeight into the kernel's bounded eventually-periodic weighted Erdos-series theorem', but the Lean statement quantifies over no engine and proves no no-go; the barrier reading is documentation, not a theorem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At every odd prime p, p does not divide A(p) = p - 2; equivalently A(p)/p is not the image of an integer in Q. Also p does not divide A(p^2) = (p-1)^2.
statement_nodes.engine: 0 < p - 2 < p for p >= 3; primality of p in Z for the square case
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary divisibility. Its value is entirely as the local input to the PrimitiveDeterminantLift index barrier; the module docstring correctly says it 'does not imply the irrationality of the #249 value'.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every natural n, the number of pairs (a,b) with a + b = n, a > 0 and gcd(a,b) = 1 equals phi(n), uniformly and with no case split (n = 0 gives the empty filter, n = 1 gives exactly (1,0)).
statement_nodes.engine: explicit bijection (a,b) -> b with inverse a -> (n - a, a) against Nat.totient_eq_card_coprime
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A bijective restatement of the definition of phi; the only content is that the half-open filter makes it hypothesis-free at n = 0, 1.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, summing r^{a+b} over coprime pairs with a >= 1 (b free) gives sum_n phi(n) r^n, and restricting to a, b >= 1 gives sum_n phi(n) r^n - r. At r = 1/2 the #249 constant is exactly the half-open coprime-pair mass, and S - 1/2 is the strictly positive coprime-pair mass.
open_antecedents: irrationality of the coprime-pair mass sum_{gcd(a,b)=1, a,b>=1} 2^{-(a+b)} is unproved and equals S - 1/2, so it is exactly Erdos #249
statement_nodes.engine: regrouping the pair power sum along addition antidiagonals through Finset.sigmaAntidiagonalEquivProd, using the visible-point count
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Generating-function form of the classical visible-point count; the probabilistic gloss (P(gcd(X,Y)=1) for fair-coin waiting times) is documentation only, no measure theory appears.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{n>=1} n r^n = r/(1-r)^2, and the totient Lambert series with its d = 1 term peeled off evaluates to sum_{n>=2} phi(n) r^n/(1-r^n) = r/(1-r)^2 - r/(1-r).
statement_nodes.engine: the totient Lambert rung minus its first term, with a dominated-summability shift lemma
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Term peeling off an already-classical identity.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, summing the strictly positive coprime-pair mass evaluated at r^{g+1} over all g >= 0 gives (r/(1-r))^2, the whole positive-quadrant mass; at r = 1/2 the layer masses sum to 1.
statement_nodes.engine: Fubini swap on the layer/antidiagonal product, then the tail totient Lambert evaluation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The identity sum_g (mass of {gcd = g}) = total mass is unique factorisation of a pair; the analytic content reduces to the already-classical totient Lambert rung. The g = 1 layer is exactly the open constant S - 1/2, so the normalisation constrains it not at all.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{d>=1} (r^d/(1-r^d))^2 = sum_n (sigma(n) - tau(n)) r^n; at r = 1/2, sum_{d>=1} 1/(2^d - 1)^2 = sum_{n>=1} (sigma(n) - tau(n)) 2^{-n}.
statement_nodes.engine: pure-squared Lambert engine with w = 1 (divisor coefficient (1 * Id) - (1 * zeta) = sigma - tau)
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The identity is a classical Lambert/divisor-series manipulation. The module docstring reads the value as zeta_q(2) - zeta_q(1) at q = 1/2 and cites the Postelmans-Van Assche q-Pade irrationality theorem, which is explicitly NOT formalised here; only the identity is machine-checked.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For 0 <= r < 1, sum_{d>=1} phi(d) (r^d/(1-r^d))^2 = sum_n (P(n) - n) r^n where P = phi * Id is Pillai's gcd-sum function; at r = 1/2 this is sum_{d>=1} phi(d)/(2^d - 1)^2 = sum_{n>=1} (P(n) - n) 2^{-n}.
statement_nodes.engine: pure-squared Lambert engine with w = phi, using phi * zeta = Id
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Pillai's gcd-sum function is classical; this is its Lambert generating identity at the squared kernel.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every positive d, the base-2 mass of the set of pairs (a,b) with a, b >= 1 and d dividing both is exactly 1/(2^d - 1)^2 — the divisibility event on the pair factorises into the two coordinate events.
statement_nodes.engine: injective reindexing (a,b) = (d(k+1), d(l+1)) and a product of two geometric series
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A two-fold geometric-series computation; it justifies the probabilistic gloss of the squared kernel but is not used in the proofs of the L2 rungs.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The sum of 1/(2^{a+b} - 1) over all coprime pairs (a,b) with a, b >= 1 equals exactly 1.
statement_nodes.engine: expand each Mersenne reciprocal as its geometric layer series, Fubini-swap, then apply the gcd-layer normalisation at r = 1/2
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Analytically equivalent to the gcd-layer normalisation after a swap; the statement is the normalisation of the reduced-slope (Stern-Brocot root cylinder) distribution. No external source located, but it is a routine in-zone corollary: the Lean proof expands each Mersenne reciprocal as its geometric layer series, applies Fubini, and then closes by literally invoking GeometricCoprimality.tsum_gcd_layer_pos_coprime_half_eq_one (the gcd_layer_normalisation node). Downgraded from not_assessed on that ground.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The closed form M(a,b) = 1/((2^a - 1)(2^b - 1)) is positive and satisfies the exact telescoping mediant recursion M(a,b) = 1/(2^{a+b} - 1) + M(a+b, b) + M(a, a+b); the two children carry at most 2/3 of the parent mass; and the depth-d finite unfolding of the recursion approximates M(a,b) from below with error at most (2/3)^d M(a,b), hence converges to M(a,b) at that explicit geometric rate.
statement_nodes.engine: field_simp/ring on 1/((A-1)(B-1)) = 1/(AB-1) + 1/((AB-1)(B-1)) + 1/((A-1)(AB-1)); induction on depth for the rate
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The split is an algebraic identity discharged by field_simp; ring, and the rate is a two-line induction from it. The docstring is explicit that the subtree-enumeration reading (that the recursion's limit really is the subtree mass under the slow-Euclid bijection) is NOT proved here, so 'cylinder mass' is a name for the closed form, not a verified combinatorial mass.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: NAMING GAP, checked against the Lean: cylinderMass is DEFINED as the closed form 1/((2^a-1)(2^b-1)) and sternBrocotDepthMass is DEFINED as a finite recursion on pairs; no declaration in this module or elsewhere proves that either quantity equals the mass of the Stern-Brocot subtree rooted at (a,b), or that the nodes enumerated by the recursion are distinct, or that they exhaust any set of coprime pairs. Every theorem here is therefore an identity/limit about two explicitly defined real-valued functions. The only point of contact with the #249 constant is that the root value M(1,1) = 1 coincides numerically with the separately proved reduced_direction_law; the coincidence is not formalised as a bijection.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Words in the two mediant moves, applied from (1,1) with the list head acting last, always reach a coprime pair with both coordinates positive; recoding a word as alternating runs of lengths n_1, ..., n_r turns the mediant action into the continuant recurrence (A,B) -> (nA + B, A), and the resulting run-boundary pair is literally the Stern-Brocot pair up to a coordinate swap for a newest right run, with equal height and the same coprimality.
statement_nodes.engine: induction on run lists with replicate-append lemmas for each direction
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The identification of Stern-Brocot run lengths with continued-fraction partial quotients / continuants is classical; this is its Lean bookkeeping.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An alternating word with r nonempty runs has run-boundary coordinates at least F_{r+2} and F_{r+1} and height at least F_{r+3}, in both run and tree coordinates; the all-unit spine attains equality, with run-boundary pair exactly (F_{r+2}, F_{r+1}) and height exactly F_{r+3}.
statement_nodes.engine: induction on the run list using n*A >= A for positive n and the Fibonacci recurrence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the continuant form of Lame's theorem: the all-ones partial quotients minimise the continuant and give Fibonacci numbers. Classical since 1844.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Writing each positive run length as 1 + e_i, the run-boundary coordinates equal their Fibonacci values plus an exactly computed nonnegative defect polynomial; deleting every mixed monomial gives a linear lower bound, the linear part dominates term by term, and the ordered linear coefficients admit the uniform floor F_{r+1} per unit of total defect, so height >= F_{r+3} + F_{r+1} * sum e_i. A single defect e at position i is exactly linear with coefficient F_{i+2} F_{r-i+1} = F_{r+1} + F_i F_{r-i-1}, and the mixed term is strictly positive as soon as the newest and some older defect are both positive.
statement_nodes.engine: structural recursion of the exact and linearised defect pairs, with the Fibonacci addition formula F_{m+n+1} = F_{m+1}F_{n+1} + F_m F_n for the one-site coefficient
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The one-site coefficient F_{i+2} F_{r-i+1} is the classical continuant splitting identity K(a_1..a_r) = K(a_1..a_i)K(a_{i+1}..a_r) + K(a_1..a_{i-1})K(a_{i+2}..a_r) evaluated on the all-ones spine. The sharp global floor is an aggregation of that. No source located for the aggregated form; the ingredients are classical.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Exact run heights at small parameters: a single run of length n has height n + 2 and two alternating runs of lengths m, n have height (m+1)(n+1) + 1. Consequently the depth-0 stratum carries base-2 mass 1/4 and the two orientations of a single positive run together carry mass exactly 1/2.
statement_nodes.engine: unfolding runBoundaryPair at depth 1 and 2, then a single geometric series
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Bounded-RUN-COUNT evaluations of the run coordinate (the run lengths themselves are universally quantified, so runHeight_single and runHeight_pair are general formulas, not bounded computations); only the first two strata are computed, and the corpus does not extend the layer computation further.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The word 'stratum' is not earned by the Lean. zeroRunMass and oneRunMass are DEFINITIONS: zeroRunMass := (1/2)^runHeight [] and oneRunMass := sum_n 2 * (1/2)^runHeight [n+1], where the factor 2 for 'the two orientations' is stipulated in the definition, not derived. No declaration in this module, in CertificateKernel (which only re-exports the two values verbatim at lines 18412-18417), or anywhere else in the repository proves that these quantities are the layers of the positive coprime-pair mass sum_{gcd(a,b)=1} 2^{-(a+b)}, nor that distinct run words give distinct pairs, nor that the layers are disjoint or exhaustive. So 'the depth-0 stratum carries mass 1/4' is a statement about a defined real number, not a proved decomposition of the #249 constant.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The sum of F_{j+2} for j < r equals F_{r+3} - 2; i.e. the natural denominator exponent accumulated along the unit-run spine sits exactly two below the minimum run-height scale.
statement_nodes.engine: induction with the Fibonacci recurrence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The Fibonacci partial-sum identity sum_{j<=n} F_j = F_{n+2} - 1 in shifted form. The module docstring is explicit that it does not assert the analytic run tail survives denominator clearing.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For the periodic tail atom omega_d(N) = 2^{N mod d}/(2^d - 1), one has 2*omega_d(N) - omega_d(N+1) = 1 when d divides N+1 and 0 otherwise: the atom doubles except at its unique wrap point, where the Mersenne numerator contributes exactly one carry.
statement_nodes.engine: case split on the wrap point with modular arithmetic and field_simp
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary base-2 periodicity of 1/(2^d - 1). Note it is not used by any other declaration in the module: the determinant theorems depend only on the definition of the atom, not on this step law.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For a square matrix whose (i,j) entry is a Mersenne tail atom of conductor d_j at index idx(i,j), the determinant equals an integer determinant of 2-power entries divided by the product of the column Mersenne denominators; hence multiplying by that product recovers an integer exactly, and whenever the integer numerator determinant is nonzero the cleared quantity has absolute value at least one. The same holds with integer column weights, the weights simply multiplying the numerator determinant.
statement_nodes.engine: Matrix.det_mul_row column factorisation plus Int.one_le_abs on the cast integer determinant
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The mathematical content is 'a nonzero integer has absolute value at least 1' applied after an exact column-denominator factorisation; both steps are routine.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out ONLY this: manufacturing a nonzero cleared value smaller than 1 from a square minor in which each column carries exactly one Mersenne denominator, when the integer numerator determinant is nonzero. It does NOT rule out: (a) the numerator determinant being zero (the degenerate case that any real attack must handle); (b) the RATIO between the cleared integer and the size of the clearing product prod_j (2^{d_j} - 1) being small, which is precisely the quantity a Diophantine irrationality argument needs — the theorem bounds the integer, never the ratio; (c) non-square or rectangular linear forms; (d) minors whose columns carry more than one conductor or a shared denominator; (e) limiting/infinite-tail constructions where the number of atoms grows with the horizon; (f) any non-determinantal certificate. It is not an irrationality statement for the totient series, as the module docstring states. MODELLING GAP: nothing in the Lean ties these matrices to #249. The conductors d, the index array idx and the weights w are arbitrary; grep confirms MersenneTailAtoms.lean never mentions primWeight, the totient, or any object from MersenneLambertLadder (which it imports but does not use), so the docstring's 'in the totient application the weights are v * A(d_j)' is documentation, not formalised content. The atom step law mersenneTailAtom_step is also unused by every theorem in the module.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The finite Mobius incidence matrix on jet coordinates q, ..., q^N, with entry mu((i+1)/(j+1)) when (j+1) divides (i+1) and 0 otherwise, is lower triangular with unit diagonal, has determinant 1, is a unit over the integers, has linearly independent columns, and its mulVec map is injective; hence the only integer coefficient vector whose companion jet vanishes at horizon N is zero.
statement_nodes.engine: Matrix.det_of_lowerTriangular on the divisibility order, unit diagonal from mu(1) = 1
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Unitriangularity of the divisibility incidence matrix and invertibility of Mobius inversion is Rota's incidence-algebra standard. Note also that IsFiniteIncidenceQuotientRelation is DEFINED as mulVec c = 0, so finiteIncidenceQuotientRelation_iff is a definitional alias of mobiusCompanionJetMap_eq_zero_iff — the 'named class' contributes no new content.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out ONLY a nontrivial integer-linear relation among the finitely many Mobius companion jets at a fixed horizon N — i.e. a rank reduction / incidence quotient of the finite jet matrix. It does NOT establish, and the module docstring explicitly disclaims, the global statement that 1, the totient series, and finitely many Mobius dilates are linearly independent over Q(q); that needs separate analytic number theory. It also does not constrain relations with coefficients in Q(q) or in a larger ring, relations involving the constant 1 or the series value itself (the matrix has no such row/column), or any relation at a horizon-independent limit. No irrationality statement for #249 follows. MODELLING GAP: the phrase 'companion jet' is not defined in Lean. incidenceMobiusMatrix N is DEFINED entry-by-entry as mu((i+1)/(j+1)) on the divisibility pattern; there is no Lean object for the Mobius companion series M_mu(q^r), no theorem identifying this matrix with the jet matrix of any actual series, and the module (which imports MersenneLambertLadder) uses nothing from it and never mentions primWeight or the totient. So the reading 'the only integer coefficient vector whose companion jet vanishes at horizon N is zero' rests on an unformalised identification; what is machine-checked is that one explicitly written unitriangular integer matrix is invertible.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For n nonzero, a positive integer D clears the normalised primitive coordinate A(n)/n (i.e. D * A(n)/n is an integer) if and only if n divides D * A(n).
statement_nodes.engine: field_simp transport between Q-divisibility and Z-divisibility
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Both sides are elementary and decidable in principle; this is a change of notation. Neither side is open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a positive integer D clears every normalised primitive Euler coordinate A(n)/n for 1 <= n <= N, then every odd prime p <= N divides D, every prime with p^2 <= N contributes p^2 to D, 4 divides D once N >= 4, and consequently the two-tier primorial lcm_{p<=N} localIndex(N,p) divides D. Hence no fixed positive integer D clears all normalised primitive coordinates simultaneously.
statement_nodes.engine: p does not divide A(p) = p - 2 and p does not divide A(p^2) = (p-1)^2, fed through Euclid's lemma in Z and aggregated by Finset.lcm_dvd_iff
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The local inputs are elementary; the aggregation into a two-tier primorial and the 'no fixed index' conclusion are a clean packaging. Not obviously a corollary of a named classical theorem, but also not obviously new — related to standard Dieudonne-Dwork integrality obstructions, which the docstring explicitly says this is NOT.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out ONLY a single horizon-INDEPENDENT positive integer index clearing A(n)/n for all n, i.e. an integral lift in the ordinary integral Euler/Witt-coordinate category. It does NOT rule out: (a) horizon-dependent indices — indeed twoTierPrimorial N is itself a candidate at each finite N, so the whole finite-jet family remains clearable; (b) any non-Euler normalisation of the primitive determinant (e.g. dividing by something other than n, or p-adic/Witt coordinates with different denominators); (c) the general Dieudonne-Dwork theorem for arbitrary integral power-series jets, which the module docstring explicitly separates from this result; (d) determinant realisations that never require simultaneous clearing. It proves nothing about the irrationality of the #249 constant.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For matrices M over a commutative ring with index types iota and kappa, det(M * N) equals the sum over all maps p : iota -> kappa of det(i,j -> M i (p j)) times the product over i of N (p i) i; non-injective maps are retained in the sum.
statement_nodes.engine: Leibniz formula plus Finset.prod_univ_sum and a sum swap
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The Cauchy-Binet expansion in its all-maps (pre-collapse) form; the docstring says it is written out only because the pinned Mathlib does not expose rectangular Cauchy-Binet.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Let s be a finite index set with an integer numerator u(i) and a natural dyadic exponent e(i) at each index. IF some m in s has odd u(m) and strictly largest exponent, THEN the cleared sum of u(i) * 2^{e(m) - e(i)} over s is odd, and in particular nonzero. The two hypotheses are free: nothing in the corpus exhibits a #249 moment family satisfying them.
open_antecedents: existence of an index m whose dyadic exponent e(m) is strictly largest in the family and whose integer numerator u(m) is odd — for the intended signed Mobius / q = 1/2 Hankel moment family this is proved nowhere in the corpus; the hypothesis is supplied, never discharged
no Lean declaration anywhere in the repository instantiates s, u, e on #249 moment data, so the implication is never fired
statement_nodes.engine: parity of a finite sum with a unique odd summand
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The standard 'unique largest 2-adic valuation' non-vanishing trick. As a general lemma over arbitrary finite data it is unconditional in Lean; but NOTHING in this zone (or, by grep over every .lean file in the repository) instantiates it on actual #249 moment data, so its hypotheses — a uniquely largest exponent with odd numerator in the real signed Mobius/Hankel family — remain unverified for the intended application. Grep counts: scaled_dyadic_sum_odd has 2 occurrences (its own declaration plus its use inside scaled_dyadic_sum_ne_zero), scaled_dyadic_sum_ne_zero has 1 (its own declaration).
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Classified conditional_implication rather than unconditional_object_theorem: the Lean statement is about arbitrary integer data (u, e) on an arbitrary finite index set and mentions no #249 object. It establishes nothing about the totient series, the primitive-conductor weight, or any Mersenne moment sequence until a family satisfying the unique-largest-odd-exponent hypothesis is exhibited, which the corpus never does. Read as a proof step for the 'signed-Hankel route', it is the conditional half of an argument whose antecedent is the entire difficulty.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Declarations only: a finite signed moment matrix over an arbitrary finite atom type, a truncated signed q = 1/2 moment sequence, and the Hankel matrix and Hankel determinant of a moment sequence. No property of any of these is proved.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Inert definitions. A repository-wide grep finds no theorem, in this module or any other, that mentions finiteSignedMomentMatrix, truncatedMoment, hankelMatrix or hankelDet. The 'signed-Hankel route for Erdos #249' named in the module header exists as vocabulary, not as proved content.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The residual-weighted monomial matrix (i,j) -> W_j z_j^{e_i} equals the monomial matrix (i,j) -> z_j^{e_i} right-multiplied by diag(W); hence its determinant is the monomial determinant times the product of the W_j, nonvanishing is preserved whenever that product is nonzero, and determinant magnitude is preserved when every W_j has unit modulus.
statement_nodes.engine: Matrix.det_mul and Matrix.det_diagonal
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Column scaling acts on determinants by the product of the scalars; textbook linear algebra.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Taking the residual weights to be the inverse pivot phases (unit modulus when the pivots are unit modulus), any row with exponent one becomes identically 1 while the coefficient-side determinant is untouched; so a nonzero minor and the presence of the locked bad first-harmonic row coexist at every rank.
statement_nodes.engine: explicit countermodel: W_j = 1/z_j, using the diagonal-gauge determinant factorisation
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The construction is one line once the gauge factorisation is available; its value is as an explicit countermodel rather than as a theorem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out ONLY residual-BLIND standalone certificates: criteria that look at rank, determinant nonvanishing, or determinant magnitude of the residual-weighted monomial matrix and nothing else, as evidence that the exponent-one row does not reconstruct the phase 1. It does NOT rule out, as the module docstring states, determinants whose rows satisfy an additional arithmetic coupling identity; nor certificates that inspect the residual values themselves, nor non-determinantal certificates, nor criteria at a fixed non-unit residual normalisation. Nothing here bears on the irrationality of the #249 constant. MODELLING GAP: ResidualGaugeObstruction.lean imports only Mathlib and never mentions the totient, primWeight, a Mersenne denominator, or any other #249 object; e, z and W are arbitrary. Which real proof strategy is being closed is therefore fixed entirely by the docstring's vocabulary ('supplier column', 'first-harmonic certificate', 'distinguished phase 1'), none of which is a Lean definition. The theorem is a true statement about arbitrary complex monomial matrices; its status as a barrier for a #249 method family is an unverified identification, and the earlier corpus incident (a barrier published as closing a method family that a weaker third engine escaped) is the precise failure mode to guard here.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Allowing the residual to vary across rows as well as columns, the explicit choice W(i,j) = z_j^{i}/z_j^{e_i} (every entry of unit modulus when the pivots are) reconstructs the ordinary consecutive-power (Vandermonde-shaped) matrix exactly, for arbitrary requested exponents; in particular its zeroth row is identically 1.
statement_nodes.engine: explicit row-dependent countermodel W(i,j) = z_j^i / z_j^{e_i}
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Strengthens the locked-gauge countermodel from column gauges to row-and-column gauges; still a one-line explicit construction.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out ONLY fixed-rank nonzero-minor certificates that are blind to a row-dependent unit residual. It does NOT rule out certificates using an additional arithmetic coupling law between rows (the module docstring says exactly this), certificates that constrain the residual by an independent identity, or any argument that does not go through minor nonvanishing. It is not an irrationality statement. Same MODELLING GAP as locked_residual_countermodel: the module contains no #249 object at all, so the identification of 'fixed-rank nonzero-minor certificate' with these arbitrary complex monomial matrices is documentation, not Lean. Note also the reconstruction is exact only for nonzero pivots (hz : z j != 0 is required), and rowReconstruction_zero_row_one constrains the row indexed 0, not the row with exponent one — the two countermodels pin different rows.
